_comment: StarryOS syscall test knowledge base. Updated by test pipeline.

bugs: sys_pwritev2 calls read_at instead of write_at (copy-paste from preadv2)
CRITICAL: sys_mmap called with MAP_PRIVATE but no MAP_ANONYMOUS → always EINVAL
Variable shadowing: user MREMAP_* flags overwritten by MappingFlags
Always creates new PRIVATE ANONYMOUS mapping, ignoring original type
Always moves mapping even without MREMAP_MAYMOVE
Shrink does not return same address
F_GETFL derives access mode from file permission bits instead of open flags
O_APPEND not tracked by F_GETFL or F_SETFL
F_SETFL only handles O_NONBLOCK
open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC|O_APPEND) fails
DATA CORRUPTION: same-file forward-overlapping copy corrupts data
flags parameter completely ignored (should reject nonzero)
No regular-file check: accepts pipes/sockets

results.notes: 1 fail is test bug not kernel bug

bugs: MAP_ANONYMOUS with fd > 0 rejected (Linux ignores fd)
Not anonymous: backed by real files at /tmp/memfd-XXXX (nlink=1, should be 0)
Data persists after close: /tmp/memfd-* files not cleaned up
memfd_create.notes: Basic functionality (read/write, cloexec, ftruncate, mmap) works correctly

bugs: Complete stub: always returns Ok(0), no actual locking performed
Exclusive locks don't block other exclusive or shared locks
Shared locks don't block exclusive locks
Invalid operation (0) not rejected with EINVAL
